evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'let's go ahead and get you quoted and I'll just you know, ask you a few questions to get us on the right track to provide you an accurate estimate and this will just take about like ten to fifteen minutes' — framing present, but rushed past without waiting for a full yes; customer says 'Okay, that's fine' but rep doesn't explicitly confirm understanding before moving forward.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into logistics probing (confirming address, house size, bedrooms) without first asking 'what are your biggest concerns about this move' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by customer in a concerns-gathering section. Customer did express a preference for a quick estimate rather than a walkthrough, but that was handled as a logistics redirect, not a concern to be explored.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Full. Rep gathered: property type (one-story house), square footage (1,395), bedrooms (3), garage (2-car, mostly storage, very full), special items (antiques, furniture), additional stops (storage unit). Also confirmed storage unit details (address, distance, indoor/outdoor, size).
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes: 'do you need help with, you know, packing the small miscellaneous items, am I right?' — asked and confirmed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes: 'At typical 1400 square footage house usually has 45 to 55 boxes. So considering that we also have stuff from the garage, roughly how many do you think?' — asked with typical anchor.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gave hourly rate ($206/hour for two movers, 26-foot truck, three movers breakdown), packing estimates ($300 materials, 5 hours labor initially, then adjusted to 1 day with 3 movers, 5 hours packing), and final estimate of '$2,926 including materials' for 7.5–8.5 hours with 3 movers. However, the estimate was not clearly personalized to the customer's stated concerns (desire to minimize antique damage, wanting photos sent for accuracy). Rep said 'in your case since you are partially moving' but didn't tie the estimate to specific customer worries.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Trip fee/materials: 'we charge an hourly rate of $206 per hour, per two movers… everything is included in this hourly rate like the fuel and tract taxes, insurance, all wrap pads and bans… The only thing outside of the early rate is the packing cost.' Hidden fees: 'there are no hidden fees of any type. No credit card fees, no transportation fees, no stair fees, no disassemble reassembly fees.' Minimum/increments: 'we have a two and a half hour minimum and once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After delivering the $2,926 estimate, rep immediately pivots to 'would you like our help with your upcoming move on Friday October 9th?' without pausing to ask 'does that feel fair to you?' or similar, and without holding silence for a reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. Rep states: 'finally we have the on time guarantee so if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and all of that is included at no extra cost.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Rep states: 'The first one is our no worries damage coverage, our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate. We provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages and like our competitors who either charge for additional coverage or offer only state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage.' — Covers the $2,000 limit, framing of 'included in our hourly rate' (not an add-on), and implicit no-deductible/no-fine-print by contrast to competitors.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. Rep delivers both promises but does not ask 'does that put these to rest?' or confirm the customer feels satisfied with these guarantees. Rep moves directly from the promise list ('and it is what keeps as one of the most awarded and highest rated moving companies around') into pricing mechanics ('now for the time. The way the clock works…').
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. At the end, rep asks: 'will there be anything else or questions for me?' — classic auto-no question, not 'what's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent genuine check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. No version of 'anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was asked.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. Rep asks plainly: 'would you like our help with your upcoming move on Friday October 9th?' — no softening or built-in out offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of rate locks, rate hold periods, or deposit structures.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. After customer declines ('I'm still gonna get some estimates from other people'), rep offers to send an email and requests photos, but does not attempt to book a move. No confirmation of date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes. Rep says 'I'll also send you an email with this information' but that is a follow-up, not a booking confirmation.

top_strength: Jevic gathered comprehensive logistics and inventory detail — property specs, garage contents, full furniture list with antique counts, storage unit location and specs — which allowed him to construct a personalized estimate rather than a generic one.
coaching_note: Never ask their agenda or concerns before diving into logistics probing; Section 2 was entirely skipped, and Section 6's final check was weak throwaway language that will not uncover remaining worries before the close.
